html:
Estonia is the northernmost of the three Baltic countries, across the Gulf of Finland from Helsinki, with Tallinn as its capital. Estonians speak a Finnic language, close to Finnish. After crusaders conquered the land in the 1200s, German landlords ruled the countryside for centuries, under Danish, Swedish and then Russian kings.

Estonia declared independence in February 1918 and defended it in a war against Soviet Russia. In 1940 the Soviet Union occupied it, as agreed in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Germany held it from 1941 to 1944, and Soviet rule then lasted until 1991.

Song kept the nation together: the song festival, held since 1869, gave its name to the "Singing Revolution" of 1987 to 1991. Estonia regained independence as the Soviet Union broke up, joined Latvia and Lithuania in NATO and the European Union in 2004, and became known for running its government online.
